description: A pure CALCULATION node — row-wise Dot, Cross and Angle Between for two vector lists. Dot measures alignment; the 2D cross is a SIGNED scalar whose sign is the left/right turn test. Draws nothing.
instructions:
A value-only node: two LISTS OF VECTORS in, one result column out. Row i of A is paired with row i of B, so a whole polygon is processed in one pass. Shapes BROADCAST, so a single vector (1×2) can be measured against an entire list. It has no geometry input or output and draws nothing on the canvas.

OPERATIONS:
• Dot (a · b) = |a||b|cos θ → an N×1 column. Alignment and projection: positive means the two point the same way, 0 means perpendicular, negative means opposing. This is the workhorse — closest point on a wall, decomposing a force along/across an axis, and solar incidence (a facade normal dotted with the sun direction).
• Cross (a × b) — in 2D the SIGNED scalar aₓb_y − a_yb_x → an N×1 column. Its magnitude is the parallelogram area, but the useful part is the SIGN: positive = left turn, negative = right turn. That single fact gives you polygon winding (sum it around a ring), convex vs reflex at each vertex, and which side of a wall a point falls on. In 3D it returns the N×3 normal vector instead.
• Angle Between — atan2(cross, dot) in DEGREES → an N×1 column. SIGNED in 2D (so it carries the turn direction) and unsigned in 3D. Preferred over acos(dot), which loses precision near 0° and 180° and throws away the sign.

INPUTS: wire vector lists into valin-a and valin-b — a point list (`val-points`), an edge-vector list (Shift Rows → Matrix Operations Subtract), or normals from Vector Ops.

OUTPUT: `val-matrix` plus `val-rows` / `val-cols`. An N×1 result feeds straight back into Matrix Operations as a PER-ROW scalar (broadcasting). Every parameter is wireable (valin-*).
